```javascript
'use strict';

/**
 * PCM helpers shared by the capture and recognition paths.
 *
 * The renderer hands us mono float samples at whatever rate the AudioContext
 * happens to be running at -- 44.1k, 48k, occasionally 96k. Every recogniser
 * we can talk to wants 16kHz 16-bit mono, so the conversion lives here rather
 * than being re-implemented by each tier.
 *
 * Two details are load bearing and easy to get wrong:
 *
 *   1. Resampling 48k -> 16k without a low-pass filter drops a signal onto
 *      itself. Every 3rd sample is taken, so content at 16-24kHz folds straight
 *      down into the 0-8kHz speech band as a phantom tone. That is audible as
 *      robotic speech and it costs Whisper real accuracy, so the decimation is
 *      preceded by a windowed-sinc FIR rather than naive sample picking.
 *
 *   2. The WAVE header is written by hand rather than by a library. It is 44
 *      bytes, the format is fixed, and pulling in a dependency for it would be
 *      a heavier trade than the code it replaces.
 */

/** Sample rate every recogniser in this pipeline agrees on. */
const TARGET_RATE = 16000;

const TAPS = 31; // odd, so the filter is symmetric and has no fractional delay

/**
 * Hamming-windowed sinc low-pass, cutoff at the new Nyquist.
 *
 * Coefficients are computed once per conversion ratio and cached: the ratio
 * only changes when the AudioContext rate does, which in practice is never
 * after startup.
 */
const filterCache = new Map();

function lowpassFor(ratio) {
  const key = Math.round(ratio * 1000);
  const hit = filterCache.get(key);
  if (hit) return hit;

  // Cutoff in cycles/sample: half the *output* Nyquist expressed against the
  // input rate, i.e. 0.5 / ratio. Slightly under 0.5 so the stopband edge does
  // not land exactly on a bin.
  const fc = 0.5 / ratio;
  const mid = (TAPS - 1) / 2;
  const h = new Float64Array(TAPS);
  let sum = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < TAPS; i++) {
    const x = i - mid;
    const sinc = x === 0 ? 2 * fc : Math.sin(2 * Math.PI * fc * x) / (Math.PI * x);
    const window = 0.54 - 0.46 * Math.cos((2 * Math.PI * i) / (TAPS - 1));
    h[i] = sinc * window;
    sum += h[i];
  }
  // Normalise to unity DC gain, otherwise the low-pass also attenuates volume.
  for (let i = 0; i < TAPS; i++) h[i] /= sum;

  const taps = { h, mid, ratio };
  filterCache.set(key, taps);
  return taps;
}

/** Band-limited resample of mono float samples to `rate`. */
function resample(input, from, to) {
  const src = input instanceof Float32Array ? input : Float32Array.from(input || []);
  if (!src.length) return new Float32Array(0);
  const fromRate = Number(from) || TARGET_RATE;
  const toRate = Number(to) || TARGET_RATE;
  if (fromRate === toRate) return Float32Array.from(src);
  if (fromRate <= 0 || toRate <= 0) return new Float32Array(0);

  const ratio = fromRate / toRate;
  const { h, mid } = lowpassFor(ratio);

  // Filter, keeping enough head and tail that the convolution edges do not
  // introduce a click into the middle of a word.
  const n = src.length + TAPS;
  const filtered = new Float64Array(n);
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    let acc = 0;
    for (let k = 0; k < TAPS; k++) {
      const j = i + k - mid;
      // Out-of-range reads are treated as silence rather than wrapped, so the
      // filter does not smear the last sample across the whole signal.
      if (j >= 0 && j < src.length) acc += h[k] * src[j];
    }
    filtered[i] = acc;
  }

  const outLen = Math.max(1, Math.floor(src.length / ratio));
  const out = new Float32Array(outLen);
  // Decimation is only valid when the ratio is a whole number. Rounding 1.5 to
  // a step of 2 would emit audio at 24k/2 = 12kHz while the header still claimed
  // 16kHz: a 25% pitch shift that turned "jumps over the lazy dog" into
  // "Feinstein southern got". Anything else interpolates, which is exact for the
  // 44.1k and 24k rates that are not multiples of 16k.
  const exact = Math.abs(ratio - Math.round(ratio)) < 1e-9;
  if (ratio >= 1 && exact) {
    // Whole-number downsampling: the filter above already removed the aliasing
    // bands, so a plain decimation is correct and keeps timing exact.
    const step = Math.round(ratio);
    for (let i = 0; i < outLen; i++) {
      const idx = Math.min(n - 1, i * step + mid);
      out[i] = filtered[idx];
    }
  } else {
    // Interpolate between filtered samples. This covers upsampling and every
    // non-integer ratio.
    for (let i = 0; i < outLen; i++) {
      const pos = i * ratio;
      const idx = Math.floor(pos);
      const frac = pos - idx;
      const a = filtered[Math.min(n - 1, idx)];
      const b = filtered[Math.min(n - 1, idx + 1)];
      out[i] = a + (b - a) * frac;
    }
  }
  return out;
}

/** Clamp to [-1, 1] and convert to signed 16-bit. */
function toInt16(float32) {
  const out = new Int16Array(float32.length);
  for (let i = 0; i < float32.length; i++) {
    let v = float32[i];
    if (!(v === v)) v = 0; // NaN would become an audible click
    if (v > 1) v = 1;
    else if (v < -1) v = -1;
    out[i] = Math.round(v * 32767);
  }
  return out;
}

/** int16 -> normalised float, the inverse of toInt16. */
function fromInt16(int16) {
  const out = new Float32Array(int16.length);
  for (let i = 0; i < int16.length; i++) out[i] = int16[i] / 32768;
  return out;
}

/** Root-mean-square level of a frame. Cheap, and enough to gate on. */
function rms(frame) {
  if (!frame || !frame.length) return 0;
  let acc = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < frame.length; i++) acc += frame[i] * frame[i];
  return Math.sqrt(acc / frame.length);
}

/** Highest absolute sample, used for reporting rather than for gating. */
function peak(frame) {
  let m = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < frame.length; i++) {
    const a = Math.abs(frame[i]);
    if (a > m) m = a;
  }
  return m;
}

/**
 * Wrap PCM in a canonical 44-byte RIFF/WAVE header.
 *
 * Both Windows System.Speech (SetInputToWaveFile) and whisper.cpp read this
 * exact layout, which is why the capture path normalises to it once instead of
 * letting each tier parse whatever it was handed.
 */
function encodeWav(float32, sampleRate) {
  const pcm = toInt16(float32);
  const rate = Math.max(1, Math.round(Number(sampleRate) || TARGET_RATE));
  const buf = Buffer.alloc(44 + pcm.length * 2);
  buf.write('RIFF', 0, 'ascii');
  buf.writeUInt32LE(36 + pcm.length * 2, 4);
  buf.write('WAVE', 8, 'ascii');
  buf.write('fmt ', 12, 'ascii');
  buf.writeUInt32LE(16, 16);        // PCM fmt chunk size
  buf.writeUInt16LE(1, 20);         // format 1 = PCM integer
  buf.writeUInt16LE(1, 22);         // mono
  buf.writeUInt32LE(rate, 24);
  buf.writeUInt32LE(rate * 2, 28);  // byte rate = rate * channels * 2
  buf.writeUInt16LE(2, 32);         // block align
  buf.writeUInt16LE(16, 34);        // bits per sample
  buf.write('data', 36, 'ascii');
  buf.writeUInt32LE(pcm.length * 2, 40);
  for (let i = 0; i < pcm.length; i++) buf.writeInt16LE(pcm[i], 44 + i * 2);
  return buf;
}

/** Duration in milliseconds, for reporting. */
function durationMs(float32, sampleRate) {
  const rate = Number(sampleRate) || TARGET_RATE;
  if (!rate || !float32 || !float32.length) return 0;
  return Math.round((float32.length / rate) * 1000);
}

module.exports = {
  TARGET_RATE,
  resample,
  toInt16,
  fromInt16,
  encodeWav,
  rms,
  peak,
  durationMs
};
```

````javascript
'use strict';

const fs = require('fs');
const fsp = fs.promises;
const os = require('os');
const path = require('path');
const { execFile } = require('child_process');

/**
 * Offline local tier: Piper.
 *
 * Piper is an optional dependency, not a bundled one -- it is a separate
 * download plus a voice model. So this tier probes for a usable install and
 * returns null when there isn't one, which lets the pipeline fall through to
 * SAPI. It must never hard-fail: on a machine without Piper this is a no-op.
 *
 * Verified behaviour on this machine: the probe correctly reports "not found"
 * and the pipeline proceeds to SAPI. The synthesis path itself is only
 * reachable once a user installs Piper and a model, so it is unverified here.
 */

const PROBE_DIRS = [
  // Development checkout: keep the runtime assets outside src/ so they can
  // be replaced without touching application code.
  path.resolve(__dirname, '..', '..', '..', 'assets', 'piper'),
  // Production: electron-builder copies this directory as an extra resource.
  process.resourcesPath ? path.join(process.resourcesPath, 'piper') : '',
  path.join(process.env.LOCALAPPDATA || '', 'Programs', 'piper'),
  path.join(process.env.USERPROFILE || '', 'piper'),
  'C:\\Program Files\\Piper',
  'C:\\piper'
];

let cache = null;
let cacheKey = '';

function candidateBins() {
  const out = [];
  for (const d of PROBE_DIRS) {
    if (!d) continue;
    out.push(path.join(d, 'piper.exe'));
  }
  return out;
}

/** Find a piper executable and a .onnx model, or null. */
async function locate(opts) {
  const options = opts || {};
  const configured = String(options.piperPath || '').trim();
  const model = String(options.piperModel || '').trim();

  if (configured) {
    const bin = configured;
    if (!fs.existsSync(bin)) return null;
    if (!model || !fs.existsSync(model)) return null;
    const config = model + '.json';
    if (!fs.existsSync(config)) return null;
    return { bin, model, config };
  }

  for (const bin of candidateBins()) {
    if (!fs.existsSync(bin)) continue;
    // Prefer a model sitting next to the binary, the usual layout.
    const sibling = fs.readdirSync(path.dirname(bin)).find((f) => f.endsWith('.onnx') && fs.existsSync(path.join(path.dirname(bin), f + '.json')));
    const modelPath = sibling ? path.join(path.dirname(bin), sibling) : '';
    if (modelPath) return { bin, model: modelPath, config: modelPath + '.json' };
  }
  return null;
}

async function probe(opts) {
  const options = opts || {};
  const key = `${options.piperPath || ''}|${options.piperModel || ''}`;
  if (cache && cacheKey === key) return cache;
  const found = await locate(options);
  cacheKey = key;
  cache = {
    available: !!found,
    bin: found ? found.bin : null,
    model: found ? path.basename(found.model) : null,
    reason: found ? null : 'Piper is not installed.'
  };
  return cache;
}

/**
 * @returns {Promise<null|{audio:Buffer,format:string,sampleRate:number,source:string,tier:string}>}
 *          null means "no local Piper; use the next tier".
 */
async function synthesize(text, opts) {
  const options = opts || {};
  const clean = String(text || '').replace(/```[\s\S]*?```/g, ' ').replace(/[*_`#>]/g, ' ').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
  if (!clean) return null;

  const found = await locate(options);
  if (!found) return null;

  const work = path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'legion-piper', `tts-${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8)}`);
  await fsp.mkdir(work, { recursive: true }).catch(() => {});
  const outFile = path.join(work, 'out.wav');

  try {
    await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      const child = execFile(found.bin, ['--model', found.model, '--config', found.config, '--output_file', outFile], {
        timeout: Math.max(15000, clean.length * 200), windowsHide: true, maxBuffer: 1024 * 1024
      }, (err) => (err ? reject(new Error(`Piper failed: ${err.message}`)) : resolve()));
      child.stdin.on('error', () => { /* piper may exit before we finish writing */ });
      child.stdin.end(clean);
    });
    const stat = await fsp.stat(outFile).catch(() => null);
    if (!stat || !stat.size) return null;
    const buf = await fsp.readFile(outFile);
    return {
      audio: buf,
      format: 'wav',
      sampleRate: readWavSampleRate(buf),
      bytes: buf.length,
      source: 'piper',
      tier: 'offline',
      durationMs: 0
    };
  } catch (_) {
    return null;
  } finally {
    await fsp.rm(work, { recursive: true, force: true }).catch(() => {});
  }
}

function readWavSampleRate(buf) {
  try { return buf.length >= 28 && buf.toString('ascii', 0, 4) === 'RIFF' ? buf.readUInt32LE(24) : 0; }
  catch (_) { return 0; }
}

function describe() {
  return {
    tier: 'offline',
    available: !!(cache && cache.available),
    reason: cache ? cache.reason : 'not probed yet',
    model: cache ? cache.model : null
  };
}

module.exports = { synthesize, probe, describe, locate };
````

```javascript
const { createVad } = require('./vad.js');

/**
 * Speech to text.
 *
 * There are three engines behind one interface, and the choice is reported
 * rather than hidden:
 *
 *   sapi-device  System.Speech opens the Windows default input itself. The
 *                engine this project has always used, and the only one that
 *                works without the renderer. It cannot be given a different
 *                microphone and it cannot be given audio we already have.
 *   sapi-file    The renderer captures through getUserMedia -- so echo
 *                cancellation, noise suppression, automatic gain and a chosen
 *                device all apply -- hands us PCM, we segment it with the VAD
 *                and write a 16kHz WAVE that System.Speech reads with
 *                SetInputToWaveFile. Same recogniser, better audio.
 *   whisper      Local whisper.cpp, when the user has installed it. Runs on the
 *                GPU when the binary reports a CUDA device it can use, on the
 *                CPU otherwise.
 *
 * The engine that used to be the only option is untouched and still the
 * fallback: on a machine with no renderer capture, or no installed speech
 * language, everything behaves exactly as it did before.
 *
 * Nothing here fabricates a transcript. Each engine returns what it actually
 * recognised or a real failure.

let capture = null;       // renderer-fed PCM session
let captureSeq = 0;

// own exit, Node reports SIGKILL with no output, which is indistinguishable
// from a real timeout unless we remember the request.
const stoppedFiles = new Set();

const PS_RECOGNIZE = `
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$stopFile = $args[0]
$maxSec  = [double]$args[1]

Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Speech

$engine = $null
try {
  $engine = New-Object System.Speech.Recognition.SpeechRecognitionEngine
} catch {
  [Console]::Out.Write('__LEGION_ERR__NO_ENGINE')
  exit 0
}

$recognizerInfo = $null
try { $recognizerInfo = $engine.RecognizerInfo } catch { $recognizerInfo = $null }
if (-not $recognizerInfo) {
  $engine.Dispose()
  [Console]::Out.Write('__LEGION_ERR__NO_LANGUAGE')
  exit 0
}

# SpeechRecognitionEngine has only SetInputToDefaultAudioDevice, and
# AudioDeviceManager is not in the public surface. The old code indexed
# GetInstalledVoices() - a list of TTS output voices - and passed a VoiceInfo
# to SetInputToAudioDevice, which does not exist; it always threw and fell
# through to the default device, so a chosen microphone was silently ignored.

# and on the sapi-file engine, which transcribes audio we captured ourselves;

$usingDefaultDevice = $true

try { $engine.SetInputToDefaultAudioDevice() } catch {

  [Console]::Out.Write('__LEGION_ERR__NO_DEVICE')

try { $engine.LoadGrammar((New-Object System.Speech.Recognition.DictationGrammar)) } catch { }

try {

try { $recognizerInfo = $engine.RecognizerInfo } catch { $recognizerInfo = $null }

}

function interpret(run, { stopped = false } = {}) {

    return { ok: false, error: { code: 'E_STT_TIMEOUT', message: 'Voice recognition timed out.' } };

    if (stopped) return { ok: false, stopped: true, error: { code: 'E_STT_STOPPED', message: 'Capture stopped before anything was recognised.' } };

    const dir = os.tmpdir();
    const cutoff = Date.now() - maxAgeMs;
    for (const name of fs.readdirSync(dir)) {
      if (!/^legion-(stt|wake)-\d+-[a-z0-9]+\.(ps1|flag|wav)$/.test(name)) continue;
      const full = path.join(dir, name);
      try {
        const st = fs.statSync(full);
        if (st.mtimeMs < cutoff) { fs.unlinkSync(full); removed++; }
      } catch (_) { /* raced with another run; fine */ }
    }
  } catch (_) { /* temp not listable; nothing to sweep */ }

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* engine: sapi-device                                                  */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

/**
 * Begin live capture from the Windows default input.
 * Returns immediately; the promise settles when recognition ends.
 */
function listen(options) {
  const opts = options || {};

    return { stop() {}, promise: Promise.resolve({ ok: false, error: { code: 'E_STT_PLATFORM', message: 'Local speech recognition is only available on Windows.' } }) };
  }
  stopActive();

  sweepOrphans();

  const stopFile = tempPath('stt', 'flag');
  const maxSeconds = Math.max(1.5, Math.min(60, Number(opts.maxSeconds) || 14));
  const scriptFile = tempPath('stt', 'ps1');

  const promise = new Promise((resolve) => {
    // The script is written to a file and run with -File, passing the sentinel
    // and the time limit as real arguments. Passing the script inline as
    // `-Command -Command SCRIPT -- sentinel seconds` does not work: PowerShell

    // whole invocation dies with "Missing expression after unary operator '--'"

    // reported "Voice recognition heard nothing" and no recogniser ever ran.
    try {

      'powershell',
      ['-NoProfile', '-NonInteractive', '-ExecutionPolicy', 'Bypass', '-File', scriptFile, stopFile, String(maxSeconds)],

        stoppedFiles.delete(stopFile);

        resolve(interpret({ err, stdout: String(stdout || '').trim(), stderr: String(stderr || '') }, { stopped: wasStopped }));

function stopActive() {
  if (!active) return false;
  const { stopFile } = active;

  try { fs.writeFileSync(stopFile, 'stop'); } catch (_) { /* ignore */ }

  setTimeout(() => {

/* engine: sapi-file and whisper                                        */

/** Transcribe an existing 16kHz mono WAVE with System.Speech. */
async function transcribeWav(wavPath, options) {
  const opts = options || {};

  // `timeout` and throws before a recogniser is ever started.
  const seconds = Math.round(Math.max(2, Math.min(60, (opts.maxSeconds || (10 + (opts.durationMs || 0) / 250)) || 20)));
  const run = await runPowerShell([wavPath, String(seconds)], { timeout: (seconds + 25) * 1000 });
  const res = interpret(run);

 * both faster and more accurate than the Windows dictation grammar, and falls
 * through to System.Speech otherwise. A Whisper failure does not end the turn:
 * the same audio is retried on SAPI, so a broken external binary degrades
 * quality instead of breaking input.
 */
async function transcribePcm(samples, options) {
  const opts = options || {};
  const inputRate = Number(opts.sampleRate) || TARGET_RATE;
  const requested = String(opts.engine || 'auto');
  const mono = pcm.resample(samples, inputRate, TARGET_RATE);
  if (!mono.length) {
    return { ok: false, error: { code: 'E_STT_EMPTY', message: 'No audio was captured.' } };
  }

  const attempts = [];
  if (requested === 'whisper') attempts.push('whisper');
  else if (requested !== 'sapi') attempts.push('whisper');
  if (requested !== 'whisper') attempts.push('sapi-file');

  let last = null;
  for (const engine of attempts) {
    if (engine === 'whisper') {
      const wav = tempPath('stt', 'wav');
      try {
        fs.writeFileSync(wav, pcm.encodeWav(mono, TARGET_RATE));
        const res = await whisper.transcribe(wav, {
          whisperPath: opts.whisperPath,
          whisperModel: opts.whisperModel,
          language: opts.whisperLanguage,
          timeoutMs: Math.round(Math.max(20000, (mono.length / TARGET_RATE) * 4000))
        });
        if (res && res.ok) {
          return { ...res, durationMs: pcm.durationMs(mono, TARGET_RATE), engine: 'whisper' };
        }
        // null means locate() found nothing, i.e. whisper.cpp is simply not
        // installed. Saying so beats a generic failure when the user explicitly
        // selected it.
        if (res === null) {
          last = { ok: false, error: { code: 'E_STT_NO_ENGINE', message: 'whisper.cpp is not installed. Install it and set the path in Settings, or choose the Windows engine.' } };
        } else if (res.error) {
          last = { ok: false, error: res.error };
        }
      } catch (err) {
        last = { ok: false, error: { code: 'E_STT_WHISPER', message: `whisper.cpp: ${err.message}` } };
      } finally {

    const wav = tempPath('stt', 'wav');
    try {
      fs.writeFileSync(wav, pcm.encodeWav(mono, TARGET_RATE));
      const res = await transcribeWav(wav, {
        maxSeconds: Math.round(Math.min(60, Math.max(4, mono.length / TARGET_RATE + 6))),
        durationMs: pcm.durationMs(mono, TARGET_RATE)
      });
      if (res.ok) return { ...res, durationMs: pcm.durationMs(mono, TARGET_RATE), engine: 'sapi-file' };
      last = res;
      // A missing language pack will not fix itself on the next engine.
      if (res.error && (res.error.code === 'E_STT_NO_LANGUAGE' || res.error.code === 'E_STT_PLATFORM')) return res;

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* renderer-fed capture                                                 */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

/**
 * Decode one chunk from the renderer.
 *
 * The renderer ships the samples as a Float32Array over a fire-and-forget
 * channel, and Electron's structured clone preserves the typed array, so the
 * common path costs no conversion at all. The Array and base64 branches accept
 * the same audio from a plain array or an encoded string; the buffer is copied
 * rather than wrapped in the base64 case because a byteOffset that is not a
 * multiple of four would make Float32Array reinterpret the bytes at the wrong
 * alignment.
 */
function decodeChunk(payload) {
  if (payload instanceof Float32Array) return payload;
  if (Array.isArray(payload)) return Float32Array.from(payload);
  if (payload && typeof payload.pcm === 'string') {
    const raw = Buffer.from(payload.pcm, 'base64');
    const copy = raw.buffer.slice(raw.byteOffset, raw.byteOffset + raw.byteLength);
    return new Float32Array(copy);
  }
  if (payload && Array.isArray(payload.pcm)) return Float32Array.from(payload.pcm);
  return new Float32Array(0);
}

/**
 * Open a capture session fed by renderer PCM.
 *
 * The session ends on the first completed utterance, on the time limit, or when
 * stopped. Audio is segmented by the VAD as it arrives, so nothing has to be
 * buffered twice and the recogniser only ever sees speech.
 */
function startCapture(options) {
  const opts = options || {};

  const maxSeconds = Math.max(2, Math.min(60, Number(opts.maxSeconds) || 14));
  const vad = createVad({
    sampleRate: TARGET_RATE,
    // A capture started while LEGION is still speaking must not transcribe it.
    frameMs: 20,
    ...(opts.vad || {})
  });

  let settle;
  const promise = new Promise((resolve) => { settle = resolve; });

  const rec = { id, vad, promise, settle, startedAt: Date.now(), maxSeconds, finished: false, reason: null, sampleRate: 0, options: opts };

  rec.timer = setTimeout(() => {
    finish({ ok: false, error: { code: 'E_STT_TIMEOUT', message: 'Voice recognition timed out.' } }, 'timeout');
  }, (maxSeconds + 10) * 1000);
  if (rec.timer.unref) rec.timer.unref();

  // A room with nobody speaking produces no speech-start and therefore no
  // speech-end, so the ceiling above is the only thing that would ever end the
  // capture. In continuous mode that leaves the microphone open for the whole
  // ceiling on every silent turn, and the mode looks stuck rather than idle.
  // Closing the turn early is what lets the renderer re-arm.
  rec.emptyTimer = setTimeout(() => {
    if (rec.vad.status().state !== 'idle') return;
    finish({ ok: false, error: { code: 'E_STT_EMPTY', message: 'No speech was detected.' } }, 'empty');
  }, Math.max(1500, Number(opts.firstSpeechMs) || 6000));
  if (rec.emptyTimer.unref) rec.emptyTimer.unref();

  capture = rec;
  return { ok: true, id, sampleRate: TARGET_RATE, maxSeconds, promise };
}

function finish(result, reason) {
  const rec = capture;
  if (!rec || rec.finished) return;
  rec.finished = true;
  rec.reason = reason || null;
  clearTimeout(rec.timer);
  if (rec.emptyTimer) clearTimeout(rec.emptyTimer);
  if (capture && capture.id === rec.id) capture = null;
  rec.settle(result);
}

/**
 * Feed audio into the open capture.
 * Returns any state change worth telling the renderer about.
 */
async function pushCapture(id, payload, options) {
  const rec = capture;
  if (!rec || rec.id !== id || rec.finished) return { ok: false, active: false };
  const samples = decodeChunk(payload);
  if (!samples.length) return { ok: true, active: true };

  const opts = Object.assign({}, rec.options || {}, options || {});
  // The frame itself carries no sample rate, so it arrives alongside it. This
  // has to be read from the options first: an AudioContext commonly runs at
  // 48kHz, and mistaking that for 16kHz would resample the speech to a third of
  // its length and shift every pitch, which reads to a recogniser as noise.
  rec.sampleRate = Number(opts.sampleRate) || Number(payload && payload.sampleRate) || rec.sampleRate || TARGET_RATE;

  // Resample once here so the VAD, the recogniser and any future engine all see
  // the same clock regardless of what the AudioContext was running at.
  const mono = pcm.resample(samples, rec.sampleRate, TARGET_RATE);
  const events = rec.vad.push(mono);
  for (const ev of events) {
    if (ev.type !== 'speech-end') continue;
    const res = await transcribePcm(ev.pcm, {
      ...opts,
      engine: opts.engine || 'auto',
      sampleRate: TARGET_RATE,
      durationMs: ev.durationMs
    });
    finish(res, 'speech');
    return { ok: true, active: false, result: res, vad: rec.vad.status() };
  }
  return { ok: true, active: true, vad: rec.vad.status() };
}

/** Suppress detection while LEGION speaks, so it cannot transcribe itself. */
function guardCapture(ms) {
  if (!capture) return 0;
  return capture.vad.setGuard(ms);
}

function stopCapture() {
  const rec = capture;
  if (!rec) return false;
  finish({ ok: false, stopped: true, error: { code: 'E_STT_STOPPED', message: 'Capture stopped before anything was recognised.' } }, 'stopped');
  return true;
}

function captureStatus() {
  if (!capture) return { active: false };
  return { active: !capture.finished, id: capture.id, elapsedMs: Date.now() - capture.startedAt, vad: capture.vad.status() };
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

function sweepTemp(maxAgeMs) { return sweepOrphans(maxAgeMs); }

/** Cached Whisper description, refreshed in the background rather than awaited. */
let whisperCache = null;

/**
 * Start a background Whisper probe.
 *
 * Deliberately not awaited by capabilities(): finding out whether an external
 * binary exists must never be on the path to answering a question about what
 * the app supports, and the first probe costs a process launch.
 */
function scheduleWhisperProbe(options) {
  const opts = options || {};
  whisper.probe(opts)
    .then((res) => { whisperCache = res; })
    .catch(() => { whisperCache = null; });
}

/** Report which recognisers are actually in use, and what they can and cannot do. */
function capabilities() {
  const sapi = process.platform === 'win32';
  const whisperReady = !!(whisperCache && whisperCache.available);
  return {
    platform: process.platform,
    sapi,
    // Stated plainly so the UI can explain it rather than offering a selector
    // that this particular engine would ignore.
    dictationDevice: 'system-default',
    selectableCaptureDevice: false,
    // The file engines are the opposite: they transcribe audio we captured
    // ourselves, so the browser's chosen device and its DSP do apply.
    fileCaptureDevice: 'renderer-selected',
    selectableFileCaptureDevice: true,
    engines: [
      { id: 'whisper', label: 'whisper.cpp (local)', available: whisperReady, device: whisperCache ? whisperCache.device : null, model: whisperCache ? whisperCache.model : null },
      { id: 'sapi-file', label: 'System.Speech (captured audio)', available: sapi },
      { id: 'sapi-device', label: 'System.Speech (default input)', available: sapi }
    ],
    whisper: whisper.describe(whisperCache),
    vad: createVad({ sampleRate: TARGET_RATE }).status().settings,
    note: sapi
      ? 'Whisper.cpp is used when it is installed, otherwise speech is recognised by the Windows recogniser from a 16kHz capture taken from the microphone selected in Settings, so that capture keeps its echo cancellation, noise suppression and automatic gain. The System.Speech engine that listens to the system default input device directly cannot be given a different device, because System.Speech exposes no capture-device API.'
      : 'Local dictation requires Windows.'
  };
}

module.exports = {
  listen,
  stopActive,
  isListening,
  capabilities,
  sweepTemp,
  // engine-agnostic transcription
  transcribePcm,
  transcribeWav,
  // renderer-fed capture
  startCapture,
  pushCapture,
  stopCapture,
  guardCapture,
  captureStatus,
  // lifecycle helpers
  scheduleWhisperProbe,
  TARGET_RATE,
  resetWhisperCache: () => { whisper.invalidate(); whisperCache = null; }
};
```

````javascript
    online: mode === MODES.PACK_ONLY ? { available: false, reason: 'pack-only mode' } : edge.describe(),
    piper: await piper.probe(options).catch((e) => ({ available: false, reason: e.message })),
    sapi: { available: process.platform === 'win32', platform: process.platform }
  };
}

function estimateWavDurationMs(buf) {
  try {
    if (buf.length < 44) return 0;
    const byteRate = buf.readUInt32LE(28);
    const dataSize = buf.length - 44;
    if (!byteRate) return 0;
    return Math.round((dataSize / byteRate) * 1000);
  } catch (_) { return 0; }
}

module.exports = { listVoices, synthesize, describePipeline, voicepack, edge, piper, MODES };
````

```javascript
'use strict';

/**
 * Voice activity detection.
 *
 * The previous pipeline had no voice activity detection at all. "End of speech"
 * was a counter inside the PowerShell recogniser that gave up after four
 * consecutive empty 0.65s polls, and continuous mode was gated by a fixed 900ms
 * timer in the renderer. Neither could react to what the microphone was actually
 * doing, and neither could see that the "speech" it had just decided to
 * transcribe was LEGION's own voice coming back out of the speakers.
 *
 * This is a small energy-gated state machine. It runs in main, on the PCM the
 * renderer captured, for two reasons: it can then be tested against synthetic
 * signals instead of a live microphone, and it sits directly upstream of every
 * recogniser, so Whisper and System.Speech both benefit from the same
 * segmentation without either of them knowing.
 *
 * Each stated failure mode maps to a specific mechanism:
 *
 *   ignore short noise    startFrames hangover -- a burst must be sustained
 *   detect speech start    frame energy over an adaptive noise floor
 *   tolerate pauses       endSilenceMs of *sustained* quiet, and the quiet run
 *                          resets the instant energy returns, so a 400ms pause
 *                          between words does not split one sentence in two
 *   avoid cutting early    pre-roll keeps the audio from before the trigger, so
 *                          the leading consonant is not clipped, and the off
 *                          threshold sits below the on threshold (hysteresis)
 *   avoid waiting too long the same endSilenceMs bounds the trailing wait, and
 *                          maxSpeechMs force-cuts an utterance that never ends
 *   ignore our own TTS    setGuard() freezes detection while the assistant is
 *                          speaking, and -- importantly -- freezes the noise
 *                          floor too, so a long answer cannot raise the floor
 *                          and make the user's next words inaudible
 */

const { rms, peak, durationMs } = require('./pcm.js');

const DEFAULTS = {
  sampleRate: 16000,
  frameMs: 20,

  // Adaptive floor. `floorInit` starts deliberately high so the very first
  // frame of a word cannot trigger on a cold estimate; it decays down within a
  // few hundred milliseconds of real input.
  floorInit: 0.02,
  floorMin: 0.0015,
  floorMax: 0.05,
  floorFall: 0.85,   // how fast the floor tracks quieter audio
  floorRise: 1.0005, // ...and how reluctantly it climbs toward a noisy room

  // Speech start: energy must clear this against the floor.
  onRatio: 3.0,
  onMargin: 0.004,
  onAbsolute: 0.0075,

  // Speech end: deliberately lower than the start threshold, so a syllable
  // dipping in energy does not end the utterance.
  offRatio: 1.6,
  offMargin: 0.002,
  offAbsolute: 0.0045,

  // A burst this short is a door slam, not a word.
  startFrames: 3,       // 60ms
  minSpeechMs: 200,
  endSilenceMs: 700,    // tolerates a natural pause, bounds the wait
  maxSpeechMs: 15000,
  prerollMs: 300
};

function createVad(options) {
  const o = { ...DEFAULTS, ...(options || {}) };
  const sampleRate = Number(o.sampleRate) || DEFAULTS.sampleRate;
  const frameSamples = Math.max(1, Math.round((sampleRate * o.frameMs) / 1000));

  let floor = o.floorInit;
  let guardUntil = 0;
  let pending = new Float32Array(0);
  let state = 'idle';

  let voicedRun = 0;      // consecutive loud frames, while idle
  let silentRun = 0;      // consecutive quiet frames, while speaking
  let speechStartAt = 0;
  // Two clocks, because they answer different questions. `totalMs` is wall
  // clock since the trigger and bounds how long a turn may run. `activeMs` only
  // accumulates frames that were actually above the release threshold, and is
  // what decides whether this was speech or a bang on the desk.
  let totalMs = 0;
  let activeMs = 0;
  let lastPeak = 0;
  let heldSamples = 0;

  let pre = new Float32Array(0);   // pre-roll ring, input rate
  const preTarget = Math.max(0, Math.round((sampleRate * o.prerollMs) / 1000));
  let held = [];                   // committed speech samples
  let heldLen = 0;

  function now() { return Date.now(); }

  function guardRemaining() {
    return Math.max(0, guardUntil - now());
  }

  /** Suppress detection for `ms`. Aborts any utterance in progress. */
  function setGuard(ms) {
    const span = Math.max(0, Number(ms) || 0);
    if (span <= 0) return 0;
    guardUntil = Math.max(guardUntil, now() + span);
    if (state === 'speech') {
      // Discard rather than emit: this audio is LEGION's own voice, and handing
      // it to a recogniser is exactly the failure this guard exists to stop.
      held = [];
      heldLen = 0;
      heldSamples = 0;
      state = 'idle';
      voicedRun = 0;
      silentRun = 0;
      totalMs = 0;
      activeMs = 0;
      return span;
    }
    return span;
  }

  function pushPre(frame) {
    if (preTarget <= 0) return;
    const combined = new Float32Array(pre.length + frame.length);
    combined.set(pre, 0);
    combined.set(frame, pre.length);
    if (combined.length > preTarget) {
      const trimmed = combined.subarray(combined.length - preTarget);
      pre = new Float32Array(trimmed);
    } else {
      pre = combined;
    }
  }

  function appendHeld(frame) {
    held.push(frame);
    heldLen += frame.length;
    heldSamples += frame.length;
  }

  function takeHeld() {
    if (!heldLen) return new Float32Array(0);
    const out = new Float32Array(heldLen);
    let at = 0;
    for (const chunk of held) {
      out.set(chunk, at);
      at += chunk.length;
    }
    held = [];
    heldLen = 0;
    return out;

  /** Feed the noise floor, but only while idle and not guarded. */
  function adaptFloor(level) {
    if (level < floor) floor = floor * o.floorFall + level * (1 - o.floorFall);
    else floor *= o.floorRise;
    if (floor < o.floorMin) floor = o.floorMin;
    if (floor > o.floorMax) floor = o.floorMax;
  }

    const on = Math.max(o.onAbsolute, floor * o.onRatio + o.onMargin);
    const off = Math.max(o.offAbsolute, floor * o.offRatio + o.offMargin);

    // energy dips would silently invert.
    return { on, off: Math.min(off, on * 0.9) };

  function endUtterance(reason) {
    const pcm = takeHeld();
    const ms = heldSamples > 0 ? Math.round((heldSamples / sampleRate) * 1000) : 0;
    const voiced = activeMs;
    heldSamples = 0;
    state = 'idle';
    voicedRun = 0;
    silentRun = 0;
    totalMs = 0;
    activeMs = 0;
    lastPeak = 0;
    pre = new Float32Array(0);

    // The gate is on *voiced* time, not on how much audio is in the buffer.
    // The buffer always carries pre-roll, so a 90ms bang would otherwise be
    // padded out to 300ms by audio captured before it even started and would
    // sail past a duration test that it should fail.
    if (voiced < o.minSpeechMs) {

      // as the start: a burst can clear the start threshold and still turn out
      // to be a door.
      return { type: 'rejected', reason: 'too-short', durationMs: ms, voicedMs: voiced, pcm };
    }
    return {
      type: 'speech-end',
      reason,
      durationMs: ms,
      voicedMs: voiced,
      peak: lastPeak,
      floor: Math.round(floor * 10000) / 10000,
      pcm
    };
  }

  function frame(frameBuf) {
    const events = [];
    const level = rms(frameBuf);

    if (guardRemaining() > 0) {
      // Consume the audio, decide nothing, and leave the floor alone.
      if (state === 'speech') {
        held = [];
        heldLen = 0;
        heldSamples = 0;
        state = 'idle';
        silentRun = 0;
        totalMs = 0;
        activeMs = 0;
      }
      voicedRun = 0;
      return events;
    }

    const { on, off } = thresholds();

    if (state === 'idle') {
      adaptFloor(level);
      pushPre(frameBuf);
      if (level >= on) {
        voicedRun++;
        if (voicedRun >= o.startFrames) {
          state = 'speech';
          speechStartAt = now();
          silentRun = 0;
          totalMs = 0;
          activeMs = 0;
          // The pre-roll is the part that stops the leading phoneme being lost:
          // by the third loud frame the first consonant is already gone.
          if (pre.length) appendHeld(pre);
          pre = new Float32Array(0);
          events.push({ type: 'speech-start', at: speechStartAt, floor, threshold: on });
        }
      } else {
        voicedRun = 0;
      }
      return events;
    }

    // state === 'speech'
    const p = peak(frameBuf);
    if (p > lastPeak) lastPeak = p;
    appendHeld(frameBuf);
    totalMs += o.frameMs;

    if (level >= off) {
      activeMs += o.frameMs;

      if (totalMs >= o.maxSpeechMs) {

        if (done) events.push(done);

      return events;
    }

    silentRun++;
    if (silentRun * o.frameMs >= o.endSilenceMs) {
      // The silence that closed the segment stays in the buffer on purpose.
      // Trimming it used to cost more than it saved: the quiet frames around a
      // word boundary dip under the release threshold, so `silentRun` reaches
      // its limit while the last word is still going, and both trimming from
      // the front and trimming from the back dropped speech. Handing a
      // recogniser a little room tone costs nothing; handing it half a word
      // costs the whole word.
      const done = endUtterance('silence');
      if (done) events.push(done);
    } else if (totalMs >= o.maxSpeechMs) {
      const done = endUtterance('max-duration');
      if (done) events.push(done);
    }
    return events;
  }

  /**
   * Feed mono float samples of any length. Splits on frame boundaries itself so
   * callers can forward browser buffers as they arrive without re-chunking.

  function push(chunk) {
    const input = chunk instanceof Float32Array ? chunk : Float32Array.from(chunk || []);

      merged.set(input, pending.length);

  function reset() {

    heldLen = 0;
    heldSamples = 0;

    voicedRun = 0;
    silentRun = 0;
    totalMs = 0;

  function status() {

      speechThreshold: Math.round(on * 100000) / 100000,
```

```javascript
'use strict';

const fs = require('fs');
const fsp = fs.promises;
const path = require('path');

/**
 * Custom voice packs.
 *
 * A voice pack is a folder of prerecorded clips plus a manifest that maps a
 * phrase to a file. Before falling back to the system SAPI engine, synthesize()
 * asks this module whether the exact phrase has a clip; if it does, the recorded
 * audio is returned instead of freshly synthesised speech.
 *
 * Matching is exact on a normalised phrase. There is deliberately no catch-all
 * or wildcard entry: playing one clip for text it does not match would show the
 * user one sentence while the app claims another, which is worse than not
 * having a pack at all. Anything unmatched goes to SAPI.
 */

const AUDIO_EXT = new Set(['.wav', '.mp3']);
const MANIFEST = 'manifest.json';
const MANIFEST_MAX_BYTES = 512 * 1024;

const state = {
  root: null,
  loaded: false,
  manifest: null,
  mtimeMs: 0,
  entries: new Map(), // normalised phrase -> { file, format }
  problems: []
};

/**
 * Where the pack lives.
 *
 * Two layouts have to work. Running from source, the pack sits beside the repo
 * root, one level above src/. Installed, the identical copy is bundled inside
 * the asar at the same relative spot -- but a user who wants their own voice
 * drops a folder beside the exe, which is where they can actually edit it
 * without repackaging. So packaged builds prefer that external folder and fall
 * back to the read-only one inside the asar.
 */
function root() {
  if (state.root) return state.root;
  const bundled = path.resolve(__dirname, '..', '..', '..', 'voicepack');
  if (process.resourcesPath) {
    const external = path.join(process.resourcesPath, 'voicepack');
    if (fs.existsSync(path.join(external, MANIFEST))) {
      state.root = external;
      return state.root;
    }
  }
  state.root = bundled;
  return state.root;
}

/**
 * Fold a phrase to its lookup key: lowercase, punctuation removed, whitespace
 * collapsed. "Yes!" and " yes " both become "yes".
 */
function normalise(text) {
  return String(text || '')
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[‘’]/g, "'")
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9'\s]/g, ' ')
    .replace(/\s+/g, ' ')
    .trim();
}

/** The filename a phrase would use if it had no manifest entry. */
function slug(text) {
  return normalise(text).replace(/'/g, '').replace(/\s+/g, '-').replace(/-+/g, '-');
}

/**
 * Keep the resolved path inside the pack. A manifest is user-supplied data, so
 * "../secrets.wav" or an absolute path must not escape the folder.
 */
function safeJoin(dir, relative) {
  const target = path.resolve(dir, String(relative || ''));
  const base = path.resolve(dir);
  if (target !== base && !target.startsWith(base + path.sep)) return null;
  return target;
}

/** Cheap sanity check so a stray text file is not handed to decodeAudioData. */
function looksLikeAudio(buf, ext) {
  if (!buf || buf.length < 12) return false;
  if (ext === '.wav') return buf.toString('ascii', 0, 4) === 'RIFF' && buf.toString('ascii', 8, 12) === 'WAVE';
  // ID3 tag, or the first MPEG frame sync.
  if (buf.toString('ascii', 0, 3) === 'ID3') return true;
  return buf[0] === 0xff && (buf[1] & 0xe0) === 0xe0;
}

/** Exact WAV metadata. Returns null for anything else rather than guessing. */
function wavInfo(buf) {
  if (!looksLikeAudio(buf, '.wav') || buf.length < 44) return null;
  const channels = buf.readUInt16LE(22);
  const sampleRate = buf.readUInt32LE(24);
  const byteRate = buf.readUInt32LE(28);
  if (!sampleRate || !byteRate) return null;
  return {
    format: 'wav',
    sampleRate,
    channels,
    durationMs: Math.round(((buf.length - 44) / byteRate) * 1000)
  };
}

async function readManifest(dir) {
  const file = path.join(dir, MANIFEST);
  const stat = await fsp.stat(file).catch(() => null);
  if (!stat || !stat.isFile()) {
    state.mtimeMs = 0;
    state.entries = new Map();
    state.manifest = { name: null, enabled: false, entries: [] };
    state.problems = stat ? ['manifest.json is not a file'] : ['no manifest.json'];
    return;
  }
  if (stat.size > MANIFEST_MAX_BYTES) {
    state.problems = ['manifest.json is too large to be a voice pack'];
    state.entries = new Map();
    return;
  }
  let parsed;
  try {
    parsed = JSON.parse(await fsp.readFile(file, 'utf8'));
  } catch (err) {
    state.problems = [`manifest.json is not valid JSON: ${err.message}`];
    state.entries = new Map();
    return;
  }
  const problems = [];
  const entries = new Map();
  const list = Array.isArray(parsed && parsed.entries) ? parsed.entries : [];

  for (const raw of list) {
    if (!raw || typeof raw !== 'object') { problems.push('ignored a manifest entry that is not an object'); continue; }
    const phrase = normalise(raw.phrase);
    const file = String(raw.file || '');
    if (!phrase) { problems.push('ignored an entry with no phrase'); continue; }
    if (!file) { problems.push(`"${phrase}" has no file`); continue; }
    const ext = path.extname(file).toLowerCase();
    if (!AUDIO_EXT.has(ext)) { problems.push(`"${phrase}" points at ${file}, which is not .wav or .mp3`); continue; }
    if (entries.has(phrase)) problems.push(`"${phrase}" is listed more than once; the last one wins`);
    entries.set(phrase, { file, format: ext.slice(1) });
  }

  state.mtimeMs = stat.mtimeMs;
  state.entries = entries;
  state.problems = problems;
  state.manifest = {
    name: typeof parsed.name === 'string' ? parsed.name : null,
    version: typeof parsed.version === 'string' ? parsed.version : null,
    enabled: parsed.enabled !== false,
    description: typeof parsed.description === 'string' ? parsed.description : null,
    entries: [...entries.entries()].map(([phrase, e]) => ({ phrase, file: e.file, format: e.format }))
  };
}

/** Load the pack if the manifest changed. Cheap and only stat()s one file. */
async function load(force) {
  const dir = root();
  if (state.loaded && !force) {
    const stat = await fsp.stat(path.join(dir, MANIFEST)).catch(() => null);
    if (stat && stat.mtimeMs === state.mtimeMs) return;
  }
  state.loaded = true;
  state.root = dir;
  await readManifest(dir);
}

/**
 * Find a clip for this phrase. Tries the manifest, then a conventionally named
 * file, then gives up so the caller can use SAPI.
 */
async function resolve(text) {
  const dir = root();
  await load();
  if (!state.manifest || state.manifest.enabled === false) return null;

  const phrase = normalise(text);
  if (!phrase) return null;

  const entry = state.entries.get(phrase);
  const candidates = [];
  if (entry) candidates.push(entry.file);
  // A pack can ship clips with no manifest entry at all, named after the phrase.
  const conventional = slug(phrase);
  if (conventional) for (const ext of ['.wav', '.mp3']) candidates.push(conventional + ext);

  for (const relative of candidates) {
    const abs = safeJoin(dir, relative);
    if (!abs) continue;
    const stat = await fsp.stat(abs).catch(() => null);
    if (!stat || !stat.isFile() || !stat.size) continue;
    const buf = await fsp.readFile(abs).catch(() => null);
    if (!buf) continue;
    const ext = path.extname(abs).toLowerCase();
    if (!looksLikeAudio(buf, ext)) continue;
    const info = wavInfo(buf) || { format: ext.slice(1), sampleRate: null, channels: null, durationMs: null };
    return {
      audio: buf,
      format: info.format,
      sampleRate: info.sampleRate,
      channels: info.channels,
      bytes: buf.length,
      durationMs: info.durationMs,
      voice: null,
      source: 'voicepack',
      pack: state.manifest.name,
      phrase
    };
  }
  return null;
}

/** Describe the pack, for the settings view and for check-voicepack. */
async function describe() {
  const dir = root();
  await load(true);
  const used = new Set([...state.entries.values()].map((e) => e.file));
  const loose = [];
  for (const name of await fsp.readdir(dir).catch(() => [])) {
    const ext = path.extname(name).toLowerCase();
    if (AUDIO_EXT.has(ext) && !used.has(name)) loose.push(name);
  }
  return {
    root: dir,
    exists: await fsp.stat(dir).then((s) => s.isDirectory()).catch(() => false),
    enabled: state.manifest ? state.manifest.enabled !== false : false,
    name: state.manifest ? state.manifest.name : null,
    version: state.manifest ? state.manifest.version : null,
    description: state.manifest ? state.manifest.description : null,
    entries: state.manifest ? state.manifest.entries : [],
    looseFiles: loose.sort(),
    problems: state.problems.slice()
  };
}

module.exports = { resolve, describe, normalise, slug, root, looksLikeAudio, wavInfo, safeJoin };
```

```javascript
'use strict';

const { spawn } = require('child_process');
const fs = require('fs');
const os = require('os');
const path = require('path');

/**
 * Wake word.
 *
 * A dedicated long-lived recogniser, separate from push to talk. It runs the
 * same Windows dictation engine, but instead of ending after a phrase it keeps
 * polling and writes every phrase it hears to stdout as a line. This process
 * watches those lines for the configured wake phrase and reports a match.
 *
 * Two properties make this honest rather than decorative:
 *   1. A phrase is only ever reported because the real recogniser produced it.
 *      There is no keyword spotting, no energy threshold and no fabricated hit.
 *   2. The wake phrase is removed from the matched text and the remainder is
 *      returned as the command, so "Hey Legion what is the weather" is one
 *      utterance rather than a wake followed by a second capture.
 *
 * The recogniser binds the system default input device, the same one push to
 * talk uses. System.Speech allows only one engine on a device, so main.js
 * suspends this listener for the duration of a capture and while speaking.
 */

const READY = '__LEGION_READY__';
const HEARD = '__LEGION_HEARD__';
const ERR_PREFIX = '__LEGION_ERR__';

const MAX_RESTARTS = 3;
const RESTART_DELAY_MS = 4000;
// A listener that has stayed up this long counts as healthy, which forgives the
// restart budget. Without this, continuous mode resets the counter on every
// resume and a crash-looping listener restarts forever.
const HEALTHY_AFTER_MS = 60000;
// After a hit, ignore further phrases briefly. The recogniser polls every 600ms,
// so the tail of one utterance can produce a second match for a wake the app is
// still acting on.
const HIT_COOLDOWN_MS = 1500;
// A listener that has not reported ready by now is hung; System.Speech can
// block forever inside Recognize() and never write a line.
const READY_TIMEOUT_MS = 20000;

const PS_WAKE = `
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$stopFile = $args[0]

Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Speech

$engine = $null
try {
  $engine = New-Object System.Speech.Recognition.SpeechRecognitionEngine
} catch {
  [Console]::Out.WriteLine('${ERR_PREFIX}NO_ENGINE')
  exit 0
}

$recognizerInfo = $null
try { $recognizerInfo = $engine.RecognizerInfo } catch { $recognizerInfo = $null }
if (-not $recognizerInfo) {
  $engine.Dispose()
  [Console]::Out.WriteLine('${ERR_PREFIX}NO_LANGUAGE')
  exit 0
}

# Same limitation as push to talk: System.Speech exposes no capture-device
# API, only SetInputToDefaultAudioDevice.
try { $engine.SetInputToDefaultAudioDevice() } catch {
  $engine.Dispose()
  [Console]::Out.WriteLine('${ERR_PREFIX}NO_DEVICE')

try { $engine.LoadGrammar((New-Object System.Speech.Recognition.DictationGrammar)) } catch { }

const ERRORS = {
  NO_ENGINE: { code: 'E_WAKE_NO_ENGINE', message: 'The Windows speech recogniser is unavailable on this machine.' },
  NO_LANGUAGE: { code: 'E_WAKE_NO_LANGUAGE', message: 'No speech recognition language is installed. Settings -> Time & language -> Speech -> Install a speech language.' },
  NO_DEVICE: { code: 'E_WAKE_NO_DEVICE', message: 'Microphone unavailable. Check that an input device is connected and enabled.' }

let desired = null;      // { phrase, onWake, onError } while the listener should run

let restartTimer = null;

 * of it, and a `\s+` between words would be defeated by a double space. Both
 * are things a real recogniser emits. So the phrase and the utterance are split
 * into words, compared word by word, and the command is taken from the original
 * words that followed the match so the user's own wording survives.

  for (let start = 0; start + want.length <= tokens.length; start++) {
    let hit = true;
    for (let i = 0; i < want.length; i++) {
      if (tokens[start + i].toLowerCase().replace(/[^\p{L}\p{N}]/gu, '') !== want[i].toLowerCase().replace(/[^\p{L}\p{N}]/gu, '')) {

function handleLine(line) {

    if (session.suspend) return;

function start(options) {

  if (process.platform !== 'win32') {
    return { ok: false, error: { code: 'E_WAKE_PLATFORM', message: 'The wake word listener requires Windows.' } };
  }

function resume() {

  // after every capture and every utterance, so clearing it on resume meant a
  // listener that crashed immediately could never reach the limit and would

  // start, or a child that stayed up long enough, forgives the budget.
  if (suspended === 0 && desired) spawnListener();

function status() {
  return {
    supported: process.platform === 'win32',
    running: !!session,
    wanted: wanted(),

    phrase: (desired && desired.phrase) || null

  let removed = 0;
  try {
    const cutoff = Date.now() - maxAgeMs;
    for (const name of fs.readdirSync(os.tmpdir())) {

    }
  } catch (_) { /* temp not listable */ }

}

module.exports = { start, stop, suspend, resume, status, matchWake, sweepTemp };
```

```javascript
'use strict';

const fs = require('fs');
const os = require('os');
const path = require('path');
const { execFile } = require('child_process');

/**
 * Offline STT tier: whisper.cpp, used when the user has installed it.
 *
 * FEASIBILITY, answered honestly
 * ------------------------------
 * The hardware is not the constraint. This machine reports an NVIDIA GeForce
 * RTX 5060 Laptop GPU with 8GB and driver 617.14; whisper.cpp transcribes a
 * ten-second utterance on hardware like that well inside a second, and even
 * CPU-only a `base.en` model stays interactive. So "can the RTX 5060 do local
 * Whisper" is yes.
 *
 * What is *not* practical is shipping it:
 *
 *   - whisper.cpp is a compiled C++ program, not an npm package. Adding it
 *     means a platform-specific binary plus a 75MB-1.5GB model file.
 *   - The npm alternatives are heavier, not lighter. `onnxruntime-node` pulls
 *     ~200MB of native binaries and needs a separate CUDA build to use the
 *     GPU on Windows; `@xenova/transformers` is CPU-only under Node and loads
 *     the model eagerly, which would block startup; `nodejs-whisper` requires a
 *     Python virtualenv, i.e. a second toolchain to install and keep working.
 *   - Downloading a model at runtime puts a network dependency on the input
 *     path, which this application has never had.
 *
 * So this tier follows exactly the rule the Piper tier already established: it
 * is an *optional* external engine, probed for, and absent means "fall through
 * to System.Speech", never a failure. Nothing is installed, downloaded, or
 * bundled, and startup is not blocked waiting to find out.
 *
 * A note specific to this GPU: the RTX 5060 is Blackwell, compute capability
 * sm_120. whisper.cpp release builds compiled before Blackwell shipped do not
 * contain kernels for it, and a CUDA build will silently fall back to CPU on
 * such a binary. That is why the probe actually *runs* the binary once and
 * reads back which device it chose, rather than assuming GPU support from the
 * presence of a driver. `--device` is only requested when the binary reports a
 * CUDA device, so a stale build produces correct results, just slower ones.
 */

  // Same layout Piper uses: a development checkout path plus the packaged and
  // user-installed locations.
  path.resolve(__dirname, '..', '..', '..', 'assets', 'whisper'),
  process.resourcesPath ? path.join(process.resourcesPath, 'whisper') : '',
  path.join(process.env.LOCALAPPDATA || '', 'Programs', 'whisper'),
  path.join(process.env.USERPROFILE || '', 'whisper'),
  'C:\\Program Files\\whisper.cpp',
  'C:\\whisper.cpp'
];

// whisper.cpp renamed its entry point from main.exe to whisper-cli.exe; both
// are in the wild and a stale folder usually still has the old one.
const BIN_NAMES = ['whisper-cli.exe', 'main.exe', 'whisper.exe'];

let cache = null;
let cacheKey = '';

function candidateBins() {
  const out = [];
  for (const dir of PROBE_DIRS) {
    if (!dir) continue;
    for (const name of BIN_NAMES) out.push(path.join(dir, name));

      : findModel(path.dirname(configuredBin));

    if (!fs.existsSync(bin)) continue;
    const model = findModel(path.dirname(bin));

}

/**
 * Run `whisper-cli -h` once and read which devices it compiled in.
 *
 * This is the only way to learn the truth about an external binary: the file
 * existing says nothing about whether it has CUDA kernels for this GPU, or
 * even whether it runs at all on this CPU. The result is cached, so the probe
 * costs one process launch per configuration, not one per utterance.

function probeDevices(bin) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    execFile(bin, ['-h'], { timeout: 12000, windowsHide: true, maxBuffer: 4 * 1024 * 1024 }, (err, stdout, stderr) => {
      const text = `${stdout || ''}\n${stderr || ''}`;
      if (err && !text.trim()) { resolve({ ok: false, reason: 'the whisper binary did not run' }); return; }

        ok: true,
        // whisper.cpp accepts --device CUDA / --device CPU. Absent a confirmed
        // CUDA device we ask for CPU explicitly rather than letting it guess.
        device: cuda ? 'cuda' : 'cpu',
        // The help text names the compiled device list; kept for diagnostics so
        // a Blackwell mismatch is visible instead of mysterious.
        devices: (text.match(/device\s*:\s*([^\n]+)/i) || [, ''])[1].trim().slice(0, 120) || null,
        version: (text.match(/whisper[_ -]?(?:cpp|cli)?[^\n]*?v?(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)/i) || [, null])[1]

/**
 * Cached availability probe. Never throws, never blocks app startup, and
 * returns a plain reason when Whisper is absent so callers can fall through.
 */
async function probe(opts) {
  const options = opts || {};
  const key = `${options.whisperPath || ''}|${options.whisperModel || ''}`;
  if (cache && cacheKey === key) return cache;

  const found = locate(options);
  if (!found) {
    cacheKey = key;
    cache = {
      available: false,
      bin: null,
      model: null,
      device: null,
      reason: 'whisper.cpp is not installed.'
    };
    return cache;
  }

  const info = await probeDevices(found.bin);
  cacheKey = key;
  cache = {
    available: !!info.ok,
    bin: found.bin,
    model: path.basename(found.model),
    modelPath: found.model,
    device: info.ok ? info.device : null,
    devices: info.ok ? info.devices : null,
    version: info.ok ? info.version : null,
    reason: info.ok ? null : `whisper.cpp was found but could not run: ${info.reason}`
  };
  return cache;
}

/**
 * Transcribe a 16kHz mono WAV buffer.
 * Returns null when there is no local Whisper, so the caller falls through.
 */
async function transcribe(wavPath, opts) {
  const options = opts || {};
  const found = locate(options);
  if (!found) return null;

  const info = await probeDevices(found.bin);
  if (!info.ok) return null;

  const args = [
    '-m', found.model,
    '-f', wavPath,
    '-nt',                 // no timestamps: we only need the words
    '-np',                 // no progress printing
    '-l', String(options.language || 'auto'),
    '-t', String(Math.max(2, Number(options.threads) || 4))

  // CPU-only build makes it abort, which would turn a working fallback into an
  // error, so the flag is conditional rather than optimistic.
  if (info.device === 'cuda') args.push('--device', 'CUDA');

  const started = Date.now();
  const text = await new Promise((resolve) => {
    execFile(found.bin, args, {
      timeout: Math.max(20000, Number(options.timeoutMs) || 60000),
      windowsHide: true,
      maxBuffer: 4 * 1024 * 1024
    }, (err, stdout, stderr) => {
      if (err && !String(stdout || '').trim()) {
        resolve({ error: String(stderr || err.message).split(/\r?\n/).find((l) => /\S/.test(l)) || 'whisper.cpp failed' });
        return;
      }
      resolve({ text: String(stdout || '') });
    });
  });

  if (text.error) {
    return { ok: false, error: { code: 'E_STT_WHISPER', message: `whisper.cpp: ${text.error}` }, device: info.device };
  }

  // whisper.cpp prefixes the utterance with timestamps even with -nt in some
  // builds, and may emit bracketed segments. Strip what is not words rather
  // than handing the recogniser's formatting to the language model.
  const clean = String(text.text || '')
    .replace(/\[[^\]]*\]/g, ' ')
    .replace(/\([^)]*\)/g, ' ')
    .replace(/^\s*[\d:.>-]+\s*/, '')
    .replace(/\s+/g, ' ')
    .trim();

  if (!clean) return { ok: false, empty: true, device: info.device };

  return {
    ok: true,
    transcript: clean,
    engine: 'whisper',
    model: path.basename(found.model),
    device: info.device,
    durationMs: Date.now() - started
  };
}

/** Drop the cached probe, e.g. after the user installs or repoints Whisper. */
function invalidate() {
  cache = null;
  cacheKey = '';
}

function describe(cacheValue) {
  const c = cacheValue || cache;
  return {
    tier: 'stt-local',
    available: !!(c && c.available),
    bin: c ? c.bin : null,
    model: c ? c.model : null,
    device: c ? c.device : null,
    reason: c ? c.reason : 'not probed yet'
  };
}

module.exports = { probe, transcribe, locate, describe, invalidate, os: os.tmpdir };
```

```javascript
'use strict';

const { contextBridge, ipcRenderer } = require('electron');

/**
 * The only bridge between the renderer and the operating system.
 *
 * Rules:
 *  - No Node primitives are exposed.
 *  - Only the listed channels are reachable; there is no generic `invoke`.
 *  - No secret ever crosses this boundary in the value direction.
 *  - Event subscriptions return an unsubscribe function.
 */

const INVOKE_CHANNELS = [
  'app:info', 'app:state', 'app:setState', 'config:onboarded',
  'window:action', 'window:setAlwaysOnTop',
  'config:get', 'config:set', 'config:reset',
  'secret:set', 'secret:clear', 'secret:status',
  'ai:status', 'ai:probe', 'ai:chat', 'ai:cancel', 'ai:profile',
  'memory:summary', 'memory:session', 'memory:list', 'memory:remember',
  'memory:forget', 'memory:clearSession', 'memory:clearAll', 'memory:export',
  'tools:list', 'tools:audit', 'tools:invoke', 'tools:confirm',
  'voice:voices', 'voice:speak', 'voice:speechEnd', 'voice:speechCancel', 'voice:listen', 'voice:listenStop', 'voice:capabilities', 'voice:pipeline', 'voice:pack',
  'voice:wakeStart', 'voice:wakeStop', 'voice:wakeStatus',
  'voice:captureStart', 'voice:captureChunk', 'voice:captureStop', 'voice:captureAbort',
  'system:full', 'shell:showItem', 'shell:openPath',
  'dialog:confirm', 'app:openExternal'
];

const EVENT_CHANNELS = [
  'state', 'metrics', 'ai:event', 'tool:confirmation',
  'timer:fired', 'app:ready', 'window:focus', 'ui:open-panel', 'shortcut:activate',
  'voice:wake', 'voice:captureEnd'
];

/**
 * Fire-and-forget channels, kept separate from `invoke` because they have no
 * reply and fire far too often to want one.
 *
 * Audio is the only high-rate channel in the app: a 20ms frame is 50 messages a
 * second for the whole time someone is speaking. Going through `invoke` would
 * allocate a promise per frame and resolve fifty of them a second for no
 * benefit. The payload is a Float32Array, which crosses the bridge as a typed
 * array by structured clone, so the samples are not base64-expanded and do not
 * show up as garbage strings in a log.
 */
const SEND_CHANNELS = [
  'voice:captureChunk'
];

const send = {};
for (const ch of SEND_CHANNELS) {
  send[ch] = (...args) => ipcRenderer.send(ch, ...args);
}

const invoke = {};
for (const ch of INVOKE_CHANNELS) {
  invoke[ch] = (...args) => ipcRenderer.invoke(ch, ...args);
}

const listeners = new Map();
for (const ch of EVENT_CHANNELS) {
  listeners.set(ch, new Set());
  ipcRenderer.on(ch, (_e, payload) => {
    const set = listeners.get(ch);
    if (!set) return;
    for (const fn of set) {
      try { fn(payload); } catch (err) { console.error(`[bridge] listener error on ${ch}`, err); }
    }
  });
}

function on(channel, handler) {
  const set = listeners.get(channel);
  if (!set || typeof handler !== 'function') return () => {};
  set.add(handler);
  return () => set.delete(handler);
}

const arg = (name) => {
  const hit = process.argv.find((a) => a.startsWith(`--legion-${name}=`));
  return hit ? hit.split('=').slice(1).join('=') : null;
};

contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld('legion', {
  app: {
    info: invoke['app:info'],
    state: invoke['app:state'],
    setState: invoke['app:setState'],
    markOnboarded: invoke['config:onboarded'],
    openExternal: invoke['app:openExternal'],
    launchProvider: arg('provider'),
```
